Project Mandela 1.1.0

Released 2026-10-13 · GitHub release · CHANGELOG.md

1.1.0 — 2026-10-13

Added

  • String value members — s.count(needle), s.splitOnce(sep), s.isBlank(), s.removePrefix(p) / s.removeSuffix(s), s.lines() and s.words(): the occurrence scan, the first-pair key=value split and the trim-to-empty test each gate in scripts/mandela/ repeated by hand. lines() splits on LF, CRLF or CR alike.
  • List value members — xs.count() (bare: truthiness count; with a predicate: indexed callback count) and xs.partition(pred), the report-and- split pair behind the gates' filter + re-filter pattern.
  • std.glob — glob.matches(text, pattern) and glob.isMatch(pattern, text): the */? matcher of the browser userscript host, exposed as a scriptable module. Segment-scan by construction, never backtracking, so it stays inside the step budget the way a regular expression could not (the guide's §12 still says no regex; this is the answer to that want).
  • scripts/mandela/changelog-check.mnd — a tenth gate: CHANGELOG.md is read by three readers (the Help Center topic, the Pages archive, the Update Manager's dialog), and a malformed header is invisible to all of them until it renders wrong. The gate reads the document the way they do — [Unreleased] first and once, X.Y.Z labels in descending order with ISO dates, only the six Keep-a-Changelog groups, no empty release.
  • scripts/mandela/todo-scan.mnd — a report, not a gate (always exits 0, like asset-report.mnd): the tree's open TODO/FIXME markers across the root notes and the Java sources the build compiles, with build output, the vendored ANTLR generator and the two trees no build compiles (lg3d-docs, the retired lg3d-awt) deliberately out — the same exemption vocabulary legacy-j3d.mnd states. Measured on this tree: 520 markers across 253 files, read out of 799,773 lines in 4,099 sources, 38 undecodable files named as the blind spot. Writing it found the sandbox's own edge: asking each line contains(marker + ":") allocates four strings a line, and over 860k lines that spent the whole 50M-step desktop(root) budget before the walk finished — the same question asked against two literal contains is what fits, with the occurrences enumerated only on the lines that mention a marker at all.
  • Guide and tables — docs/mandela-language.md documents every member above in the Str/List tables and carries a new §9 section for std.glob, with its code fence compiled by DocumentationTest.
  • The suite that proves it — 117 cases (1142 → 1259 in the module's one test task): every new member answered from a script, std.glob read at its edges (a candidate shorter than its pattern, a tail whose ground the head already consumed, consecutive stars, a starless literal mismatch), and the two-arity count callback indexed like map's. Writing them is what found the matcher's one real defect: the head segment was cut by where the pattern's first star sits without asking the text how long it was, so glob.matches("a", "abc*") threw an index error instead of answering false. The bound is now checked before the walk, and the run's length is derived from the segment rather than passed beside it — which is how the mistake became unrepresentable rather than merely untested.

Changed

  • The artifact name is lg3d-mandela-1.1.0.jar; Mandela.IMPLEMENTATION_VERSION and the manifest's Implementation-Version follow it. mandela-version.mnd gates all eight copies over the bump.
  • The module's JaCoCo floor moves with the numbers it is set under: 0.905 / 0.800 → 0.910 / 0.815 (measured 91.49 % line / 81.86 % branch). rt/StandardLibrary stays at every line covered, and the new members' branches are covered from both sides rather than only the true half — the two outcomes that hid the glob defect and the carriage return that ends a text are both line-covered today and were both wrong yesterday, which is the argument for pinning branches and not lines.

The test reports of a published release are generated beside this page: <version>/reports/ carries the JUnit, JaCoCo, Cucumber and PIT mutation reports of every module with a test suite. Each module runs report-only (mutationThreshold = 0, no gate) unless it appears in the mutationExemptions map, where it is gated at the score its own suite really achieves. The same tree is attached to the GitHub release as reports-<version>.zip, so a report outlives a rebuilt site.
